title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages. K is a field with absolute Galois group Γ = Gal(K̄/K). X is a K-scheme (the motivating case is an anabelian curve) and I is a finite set of K-rational points. Γ acts on the profinite fundamental groupoid Π̂_1(X_K̄, I), fixing the objects. For a path l : x → y and u ∈ Γ, u(l) is again a path x → y. Two discrepancy elements are defined:
- g_l(u) = u(l)·l⁻¹, which lies in π̂_1(X, y);
- f_l(u) = l⁻¹·u(l), which lies in π̂_1(X, x).
Write l(γ) = lγl⁻¹ for transport of a loop along l.

Previous page, formula (10). For x →l' y →l'' z: g_{l''l'}(u) = g_{l''}(u) · l''(g_{l'}(u)). This is multiplicativity in the path.

This page, formula (11). The analogue for f, with l' : x → y and l : y → z: f_{ll'}(u) = l'⁻¹(f_l(u)) · f_{l'}(u). Grothendieck notes it is equivalent to (10) but 'un peu moins sympathique'.

Crossed-out passage. It claims that (10) says g_l, for fixed l and u varying, is a 1-cocycle Γ → π̂_1(X, y) for the natural Γ-action. The associated left π̂_1(X, y)-torsor is Hom_{Π̂_1}(x, y), with π̂_1(X, y) = Hom(y, y) acting by composition. This is the path torsor P(x, y) and its Galois class: what is now called the non-abelian Kummer (Kim) map, and the starting point of the section conjecture.

Formula (12). For a composable chain x_0 →l_1 x_1 → … →l_n x_n, (10) iterates to: g_{l_n…l_1}(u) = g_{l_n}(u) · l_n(g_{l_{n-1}}(u)) · (l_n l_{n-1})(g_{l_{n-2}}(u)) ⋯ (l_n⋯l_2)(g_{l_1}(u)).

End of page. He remarks that this is the simplest form one could hope for, and announces a context in which (12), its f-analogue and formulas (9) become much simpler. On the next page that context is a 1-connected space T → X. Its points give a transitive system of isomorphisms between the fundamental groups at different base points, so that g and f become one and the same element of a single group π = π_1(X; T). This is an extended 'base-point set', a precursor of Deligne-style tangential or contractible-region base points used for GT-type computations.

Purpose: bookkeeping for how the Galois action on finitely many generating paths determines the action on all paths. This serves the question raised on the previous page of whether the action on Π̂_1(X_K̄, I) determines u.
errors: The crossed-out claim that formula (10) expresses the 1-cocycle property is a confusion. (10) is a relation in the path variable l, not in u ∈ Γ. The cocycle property is a separate fact: g_l(uv) = u(g_l(v))·g_l(u), a cocycle up to the order/side convention. Grothendieck presumably struck the passage for this reason; the torsor identification itself is correct.
Notational inconsistency: the notations g_l(u) and g_u(l), and f_l(u) and f_u(l), are used interchangeably. Formulas (10), (11) and (12) otherwise check out.

ideas.what: Galois discrepancy g_l(u) = u(l)l⁻¹ of a path between rational points, and its multiplicativity/transport formulas (10)–(12)
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the profinite path groupoid; elementary groupoid-cocycle calculus
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Galois action on fundamental groupoids, without these formulas

ideas.what: Path set Hom(x, y) as a Galois-equivariant π̂_1(X, y)-torsor, classified by the cocycle u ↦ g_l(u) (crossed-out passage)
ideas.modern_name: path torsor / non-abelian Kummer map / section-conjecture cocycle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings, 1983); later Kim (2005) and others
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), in Geometric Galois Actions I (1997)

ideas.what: Announced reduction (next page) using a 1-connected T → X to put all base points into one group π_1(X; T)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group relative to a simply connected set of base points (cf. tangential base points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989) and Ihara for tangential base points; Brown for groupoids on sets of base points

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of routine groupoid-cocycle identities, all correct. The struck-out torsor remark is the well-known path-torsor/section-conjecture viewpoint that Grothendieck himself published in his letter to Faltings. Nothing new for specialists.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out passage begins 'La formule (10) peut s'exprimer en disant que pour l fixé, u ∈ Γ variable,'. The formula number written there is likely (10), not (16).

The final lines read approximately: 'Formule la plus simple possible au demeurant [?] qu'on pourrait imaginer… Or nous développerons un contexte qui permette d'écrire cette formule, ainsi que (11), la formule analogue sur f et les formules (9)…'. The words 'au demeurant' and 'développerons' are uncertain readings.
